Lod
LOD
proper noun
Hebrew lod, perhaps “travail” or “strife,” a town built by the Benjamites, resettled by the returning captivity, and known in the New Testament as Lydda.

Biblical Definition

Lod was a town first builded by the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin, who builded Ono and Lod, with the towns thereof (1Ch 8:12). After the long captivity in Babylon the men of Lod were numbered among those who returned with Zerubbabel to dwell again in the land of their fathers (Ezr 2:33), and Lod with its towns is named among the places where the children of Benjamin settled after the return (Neh 11:35). In the days of the New Testament the town was called Lydda, and there the apostle Peter came down to the saints and healed Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years sick of the palsy, saying, Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole; and all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord (Act 9:34). The dictionary marks how the LORD kept this one town through the centuries, from the building of the Benjamites, through the ruin of the captivity, unto the resettling of the remnant, and at the last made it a place where the gospel was preached and a whole region turned to Christ. Lod stands as a witness to the faithfulness of God over the long generations, who plants a people, and brings them home from exile, and visits them in the fulness of time with the salvation of His Son.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town built by the Benjamites, resettled after the captivity, known in the New Testament as Lydda.

expand to see more

LOD, a town built by the sons of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin.

The name perhaps signifies “travail” or “strife.”

Its men returned from the Babylonian captivity with Zerubbabel.

It was resettled by the children of Benjamin after the return.

It is the Lydda of the New Testament, where Peter healed Aeneas.

Key Scripture

1Ch 8:12 — "The sons of Elpaal; Eber, and Misham, and Shamed, who built Ono, and Lod, with the towns thereof:"

Ezr 2:33 — "The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty and five."

Neh 11:35 — "Lod, and Ono, the valley of craftsmen."

Act 9:34 — "And Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately."

Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the faithfulness of God over the long generations of His people.

expand to see more

Lod is a town of the sacred record, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name in the building of Benjamin, in the return of the captivity, and in the journeys of Peter may know it for a real town kept by a real God through the centuries.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the faithfulness of God over the long generations of His people. He who set the Benjamites to build Lod is the same who brought its men home from Babylon and at the last sent the gospel thither in the days of the apostles. The saint who fears that the LORD’s purpose may fail across the years may remember Lod, builded, exiled, restored, and visited with the salvation of Christ.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew, perhaps “travail,” Lod names a Benjamite town, the Lydda of the New Testament.

"Like Lod, builded and exiled and restored, the church is kept by God across the long generations."

"The LORD who brought the men of Lod home from Babylon visited them at the last with the gospel of His Son."
